raw.assessment: The incumbent combines quick scheduled production with coordinator reconciliation against varied schedules. It achieved 32/40 intended course sets and 17-minute median handling, missing both targets. Unchanged-assignment files had a seven-minute median, supporting a change-sensitive failure hypothesis without proving causation. Six affected exports involved reassignment, but the two renamed-course cases limit an assignment-only account. Replacement turnaround greatly exceeds execution time; its contribution to active handling is unmeasured. Zero observed cross-center rows provides bounded reassurance: the split-course center was absent. All explanations below remain hypotheses.

openings.claim: Using current assignments or mutable names to resolve a requested week may create either actual membership errors or apparent omissions during comparison.
openings.delta: Distinguish missing course identities from correct identities displayed under unexpected names before choosing a historical-assignment or naming remedy.
openings.prediction: A temporal-membership fault changes exported identity sets after reassignment; a naming fault preserves those sets while coordinators flag a mismatch. If neither pattern appears, both explanations lose support.
openings.probe: In private staging, use fabricated records and coordinator-agreed expected weekly sets. Compare unchanged, midweek-reassigned, renamed, and split-course fixtures while attendance entry continues. Inspect internal identities and center ownership alongside the unchanged CSV schema.
assumptions: Expected weekly membership can be agreed despite differing timetables.
Fabricated fixtures and internal identity inspection fit the six-day allowance.

openings.claim: Which coordinator actions account for handling above twelve minutes: reconciliation, replacement requests, or spreadsheet import?
openings.delta: Measure active work separately from replacement waiting to identify whether faster reruns could improve the handling target.
openings.prediction: If replacement administration dominates active work, its removal saves handling time; if checking or importing dominates, faster delivery mainly reduces elapsed delay.
openings.probe: Use the six coordinators’ two short sessions with fabricated weekly files. Time checking, requesting, downloading, and importing separately; compare a replacement-request exercise with a replacement already available. Retain only aggregate timings inside authorized workspaces.
assumptions: Exercises approximate ordinary actions; results require subsequent validation across forty weekly exports.
Sessions and analysis remain within existing resources.

raw.assessment: The awkward cases are the two rename-associated exports alongside six reassignment-associated exports; unchanged assignments had lower handling time. The observations do not establish whether courses were absent from raw CSV, lost during import, or misrecognized. Both explanations below are hypotheses. Probe only with fabricated staging data and authorized coordinator workspaces, retain the documented CSV schema, permit concurrent attendance entry, and cap work at six engineer-days within existing hosting. Sampled non-leakage does not establish isolation for the unobserved split-course case.

openings.claim: Export membership may depend on mutable current assignment or course-label joins rather than requested-week course identity. Reassignment and renaming could therefore omit courses, while unchanged courses retain matching joins.
openings.delta: The rename anomaly suggests a shared identity-resolution defect broader than instructor timing alone.
openings.prediction: Against an agreed requested-week course set, affected courses are already missing or misgrouped in raw CSV before spreadsheet import; matched unchanged courses remain present.
openings.probe: Create fabricated matched fixtures differing only in a midweek reassignment or rename. Keep requested week and attendance fixed. Compare raw exported course membership before and after each change, then inspect the relevant selection joins if membership changes.
assumptions: Fabricated fixtures can represent course identity independently of displayed labels.
Current labels or assignments participate in selection or joins; this is unverified.

openings.claim: Course records may survive export, while changed labels or instructor attribution break spreadsheet matching or coordinator recognition against local schedules. Stable assignments avoid this reconciliation burden.
openings.delta: The apparent absence could arise after export, explaining both rename and reassignment cases without raw membership loss.
openings.prediction: Raw CSV contains the agreed course set, but courses disappear during import or are judged absent during comparison; showing a verified old-to-new identity mapping reduces the latter errors.
openings.probe: In the two short sessions, observe consenting coordinators importing and checking fabricated changed and unchanged files. Agree expected courses first; record raw membership, imported membership, recognition errors and handling time separately. Counterbalance presentation of an identity mapping.
assumptions: Fabricated schedules can approximate coordinators' actual checking methods.
Display fields influence import matching or recognition; neither behavior was observed in the supplied sample.

openings.claim: Current assignments or mutable-label joins may omit or misgroup requested-week courses.
openings.discriminator: Raw identities change after reassignment or rename versus unchanged controls.
openings.probe: Fix week/attendance; agree expected sets; compare unchanged, reassigned, renamed and split fixtures. Inspect identities, center ownership and implicated joins during attendance entry.
openings.uncertainty: Causality and joins unverified; timetables uncertain; split-center isolation unsampled.

openings.claim: Correct raw membership may become import loss or apparent absence through changed labels/attribution.
openings.discriminator: Separate raw membership, imported membership and recognition; mapping helps recognition errors.
openings.probe: Six coordinators, two short sessions each: observe fabricated changed/unchanged files against agreed schedules; counterbalance verified old/new identity mapping.
openings.uncertainty: Import/recognition behavior unobserved; exercises may misrepresent local methods.

openings.claim: Replacement administration may dominate handling; faster delivery may only reduce waiting.
openings.discriminator: Separate active checking, requesting, downloading and importing from replacement delay.
openings.probe: In those sessions, compare requesting replacements with replacements already available; retain aggregate timings.
openings.uncertainty: Contributions unmeasured; exercise effects require weekly validation.

lineage.reason: Retains actual membership versus apparent naming errors.

post_distill.decision: Probe before choosing remedies. Use fabricated private staging and authorized workspaces, documented CSV, concurrent entry, six engineer-days and existing hosting. Validate 40 weekly exports: median handling <=12 minutes, intended sets >=95%, zero foreign-center records; sampled non-leakage is insufficient.
